resources.string: Use this tablet and S Pen as a drawing tablet for your Windows PC.

1. On the PC, run Slate (it sits in the notification area).
2. On this tablet, turn on Developer options: Settings › About tablet › Software information › tap Build number 7 times.
3. Settings › Developer options › turn on USB debugging.
4. Plug the tablet into the PC and tap Allow on the USB debugging prompt.
The tablet connects by itself and opens the drawing surface.
Looking for PCs running Slate on this network…
Enter the 4-digit code shown in Slate on the PC (right-click its icon in the notification area).

Smaller means less hand movement for the same distance on the PC screen: only the middle of the tablet is used. To go the other way (more hand movement, finer detail), choose a smaller region of the screen in the PC settings instead.
Tip: if pressing the S Pen button opens Air command, turn it off in Settings › Advanced features › S Pen › Air command so the button reaches the PC.

On the drawing surface, tap Write on the right edge. Write sentences or equations; tap Enter and the PC types the text into whatever text field is selected. Equations come out as Unicode (x², √, π). Uses Claude Sonnet 5.5 through your own Anthropic API key from console.anthropic.com, billed to that account at roughly a third of a cent per conversion (the calculator uses Claude Opus 5.5, about 1–3¢). The writing image goes to Anthropic.
Fast handwriting (Claude Haiku 4.5: about twice as fast and a third of the price, but misreads messy writing and harder maths more often)
Add a space after each converted piece of text
API spend this month: about $%1$.2f (%2$d requests). Handwriting ≈ 0.3¢, calculator ≈ 1–3¢ each.

Handwriting in any app on this tablet: write with the S Pen and tap Enter to put the text in the selected field. Turn it on once. Step 3 adds a "✎ Slate" button above Samsung Keyboard (or any other keyboard) that switches to Slate Keyboard in one tap; ⌨ on Slate Keyboard goes back.

In the list that opens, tap Installed apps › Slate helper › On. It adds the ✎ Slate button above other keyboards and lets Ask Claude capture the tablet\'s screen without asking each time. If you turned it on before an update, turn it off and on again once. If Android says it\'s a restricted setting: Settings › Apps › Slate › ⋮ (top right) › Allow restricted settings, then try again.
✎ Slate button above other keyboards, and Ask Claude screenshots without a prompt.

Slate helper does two things. It shows a small ✎ Slate button just above Samsung Keyboard or any other keyboard while it is open; tap it to switch to Slate Keyboard. For that it only looks at where the keyboard is on screen and which keyboard it is. And when you tap Ask Claude (Air command, the Quick Settings tile or the app icon), it takes one screenshot of the screen so you don\'t get Android\'s screen-capture prompt every time. It never captures the screen at any other time and never reads what you type. The screenshot is only sent anywhere when you ask your question.
Screen mode (the PC\'s screen on the tablet)

On the drawing surface, tap Screen. The S Pen works as a pen right on the picture. Fingers: tap = click, hold = right-click, drag = drag, two fingers = scroll (or pinch to zoom the view), three-finger swipe left/right = switch apps, up = task view, down = desktop. ⋯ View has fit / shrink / zoom, real Windows touch, follow-the-cursor, monitor and quality. The first time, the PC downloads a video encoder (about 115 MB). Shortcut buttons down the left edge, one Label=Keys per line:

In Screen mode tap Ask: the PC\'s screen freezes so you can circle or highlight things and write your question, then tap Explain, Step by step, Just a hint, Check my working or Quiz me (or Ask). With the PC connected, questions go to a Claude Code session or the Claude Desktop app (chosen in Slate\'s PC settings), which you can open in the Claude apps. For the tablet\'s own screen, add "Ask Claude" to the S Pen\'s Air command (Air command › Add shortcuts › Ask Claude), add the "Ask Claude" tile to Quick Settings, or share a screenshot to Slate; without a PC these are answered by Claude Opus 5.5 with your API key.
The floating chat box is on: answers appear in it, on top of whatever you\'re looking at.
Claude Code on this tablet (your Claude subscription)

Without the PC, Ask can use Claude Code running in Termux on this tablet, signed in with your Claude subscription, instead of the API key. One-time setup: install Termux and Claude Code (npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code, then run claude once to sign in). Tap Set up (it copies a command), paste it into Termux and press Enter, then run slate-claude there whenever you want to use it (leave Termux open).
✓ Claude Code in Termux is connected.
Claude Code in Termux isn\'t running (start it with slate-claude).
Set up Claude Code in Termux

The setup command is copied. In Termux, long-press › Paste, then press Enter. It installs Slate\'s bridge (Node.js too if needed).\n\nThen run slate-claude in Termux and leave it running. Slate\'s main screen shows ✓ when it connects.
Ask may use the API key when neither the PC nor Claude Code is available
Handwriting and calculator through Claude Code too (uses your subscription; about 3–5 s per conversion instead of 1–2 s)
Not connected. Waiting for the PC over USB, or pick a PC below.
Swipe in from an edge and go back to leave.
